analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 17, 2026)
key_insights: Sales commentary, not research. JPM Market Intel is Tactically Bullish into year-end. It argues positioning is cleaner and entry points are more attractive after the tech washout, with NVDA earnings (Nov 17 after the close), capital markets activity and the JPM APAC Tech Conference as the catalysts.

Macro driver is the Fed reaction function. Growth is above trend and inflation is accelerating again after last week's hot CPI. JPM says this raises the question of the neutral rate and whether the Fed falls behind the curve in 2027, turning tightening risk into liquidity risk for risk assets.

Premarket futures were lower (SPX -0.3%, NDX -0.3%, RTY -0.5%) with Mag7, memory, semis and software weakest. The 10Y was at 5.097% and VIX at 23.52. The curve bull steepened, with yields down 2-4bp. Yesterday's sell-off came on low volume.

NVDA is the focus. Josh Meyers (TMT Spec Sales) reports buyside frustration over Jensen Huang's behavior and departure as CEO, uncertainty over a successor (Rene Haas and Lip-Bu Tan mentioned), and a view that China hawks are pushing to close export channels. Petitions to bring Huang back are also circulating. Some bulls think the bench is deeper than assumed.

JPM Equity Derivatives (Friday flash note) says NVDA hedging flows that amplified recent swings are fading (less dealer gamma, lower skew) while sentiment is bullish. Options carry little fear of a large drop into earnings, so the move depends on the earnings surprise. Trades flagged: buy Mar-27 115%-130% call spreads for 0.77%, take profits on structured-product-aligned vol trades, avoid short gamma into earnings, buy semis sector dispersion at historical lows.

Mike Feroli expects Retail Sales of 0.0% MoM headline, 0.3% ex-autos and 0.3% ex-autos and gas, down from +0.8%, +0.9% and +0.2% last month. He cites fading tax-stimulus spending and high gas prices. YoY figures were not published because of the October 2025 government shutdown.

US Market Intel counters the weak-consumption read: consumer cash is up $7.9T (+53.8%) and household net worth up $78T (+72.5%) from 2019Q4 to 2026Q2. A downside Retail Sales print could feed the recession narrative (recession basket +15.8% QTD vs SPX -1.2%), while an inline or stronger print would shift flows to Beta and Cyclicals.

JPM APAC Tech Conference Day 1 (Matt See): the audience was neutral on growth with only 5% worried about recession. AI capex was named the main swing factor by 50% and geopolitics by 30%. Investors were downbeat on tech while corporates cited robust demand. Concern was widespread that interim CEO Kress will give a cautious guide for fiscal 2027. Tech sold off (Advantest -11%, Hynix -8%, TSMC -6%).

Panel takeaways were mostly bullish: hyperscalers are expected to spend close to $10tr on compute, frontier models are released every 16 days, token costs are down 98% while GPU prices keep rising on scarcity, and value is expected to shift from infrastructure to applications. Silicon Data plans to launch compute futures on CME.

Flows: equity ETFs drew $74.6Bn (2.7z, strongest in at least 5 years), led by US ETFs at $65Bn. About 20% of US inflows were CIB-related creations that may reverse this week. Levered semis ETFs saw heavy outflows (SOXL -$3.7Bn, SOXS -$1.8Bn), while SMH (+$1.9Bn) and NVDL (+$0.7Bn) drew buying. Treasuries (-$4.2Bn), Munis (-$0.8Bn) and crypto ETFs (-$1.6Bn) saw outflows.

CTAs likely remain neutral to short US equities, with SPX, NDX and RTY about 3-4% below the momentum signals that could trigger releveraging. They likely sold long-dated USTs after the hot CPI and added to shorts in precious metals and crypto. CFTC data show Asset Managers covering VIX shorts and Leveraged Funds cutting SPX shorts.

Bear case from US Market Intel: AI and tech take another leg lower, retail and buyback bids fade, Fed narrative turns hawkish (17 Fedspeakers this week, some discussing a 50bp move vs the 4 hikes priced including December), and positioning has not yet purged (US positioning ~20th percentile, global semis exposure 80th percentile).

Dubravko Lakos-Bujas reiterates his year-end 2026 SPX target of 8,000 ($365 EPS, 21.9x), 8.4% above Friday's close. Trade ideas: long 12M momentum vs short 3M momentum, Low Vol less compelling (prefers Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples), AI upstream attractive after the positioning flush, Consumer Cyclicals challenged near term.

Updated Monetization Menu (Nov 16): move back toward tech with primary exposure to Mag7 and options to play an AI rebound, prefer Cyclicals over Defensives, and favor Europe for Cyclical/Value exposure, though a stronger USD could temper it. JPM says nominal GDP growth drives SPX earnings, so higher inflation is not a near-term earnings problem.

market_movers.rationale: Earnings on Nov 17 come with uncertainty over leadership after Huang's exit and over China export restrictions, and the buyside fears a cautious fiscal 2027 guide. JPM Equity Derivatives sees options priced with little fear of a large drop, so the move depends on the surprise.

sector_views.rationale: US Market Intel favors moving back toward tech with Mag7 as the core exposure and options for an AI rebound. It sees the washout as at or near completion but flags risk of another semis decline.
JPM prefers Cyclicals over Defensives as the growth narrative reboots and markets absorb a more hawkish Fed.
Relative positioning and valuation favor European cyclicals over US counterparts, though a USD surge could temper outperformance.
Within Low Vol, Dubravko sees the best opportunity in Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples. Low Vol overall is less compelling after moving from the 0th to the 25th percentile.

Affordability is a headwind tied to oil prices, borrowing costs and housing shortages. Longer term he sees value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail vs Energy, and mortgage rates need to approach 6.0% for housing inflows.

earnings_insights: NVDA reports Tuesday Nov 17 after the close (fiscal Q3 2027). JPM Equity Research frames the debate around leadership uncertainty and China regulatory risk. The buyside fears a cautious fiscal 2027 guide from interim CEO Kress, described as a post-Huang kitchen sink. Buyside bars were shown as a chart not reproduced in the text.
Other US earnings: Nov 17 DIS, HD, KPTIQ, NVDA. Nov 18 LOW, P, PANW, TGT, TJX, WWD. Nov 19 INTU, KEYS, ROAD, ROST, WMT, WSM. Nov 20 BMNR, CPRT, IESC, VEEV.
Wuxi Biologics: the protein service segment grew +40% y/y in 1H and the second half is guided stronger. The segment was recently broken out of total revenues given investor interest.

vol_and_positioning: VIX at 23.52 in the premarket update.
NVDA: JPM Equity Derivatives sees dealer gamma and skew falling, hedging flows fading, sentiment bullish and little fear of a large drop priced into earnings.

Hedge funds have been sellers for 6 consecutive weeks, a Positioning Intel record. Aggregate US positioning is ~20th percentile in the Tactical Positioning Monitor (since 2015) and global semis exposure is 80th percentile, so no definitive positioning purge yet.

CTAs neutral to short US equities, 3-4% below momentum triggers. Likely long European equities, short APAC (ex-Australia and India), short global rates (ex-China and Korea), short Energy (ex-natgas), long USD vs global FX.
Futures: MSCI EM saw strong selling (-3.8z), large net selling in MID, DAX, Germany 5y/10y and SOFR, large net buying in AUD futures.

CFTC: Asset Managers sold EAFE, covered VIX shorts (+2.8z) and added to UST 10y futures. Leveraged Funds cut SPX shorts, flipped long EAFE (+2.3z) and sold USTs. Managed Money sold oil and bought gold.
Levered ETF outflows of -$5.2Bn (-2.2z) driven by semis de-grossing, while NVDL took in ~$0.7Bn on dip buying.
geopolitical: Buyside talk of China hawks (led by Rubio?) moving to shut the door on exports to China, with Trump under pressure to out-hawk them, seen as negative for open source models and potentially for NVDA.
APEC Economic Leaders Meeting in Shenzhen, China, Nov 18-19.
US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027.
US Government Funding deadline Dec 11 and G20 Summit in Miami Dec 15-16.
Investors in the APAC conference survey ranked geopolitics second (30%) as the big swing factor.

tension_points.bull_case: NVDA reiterates capex and support for existing financing deals and gives clarity on leadership. Equity Derivatives notes flows have shifted from downside protection to playing for upside surprises, and JPM expects a tech rebound led by hedge funds after 6 weeks of selling.
tension_points.bear_case: NVDA fails to reassure on AI ecosystem financing, more disclosures follow Huang's ouster, capital markets events are delayed or APAC conference pre-announcements disappoint, sending AI and tech another leg lower.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NVDA failing to reiterate capex and support for existing financing deals at the Nov 17 earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: An inline or stronger print shifts flows back toward Beta and Cyclicals. Consumption levels stay high on large consumer cash balances and full employment.
tension_points.bear_case: A downside print (headline 0.0% expected) fuels the recession narrative, with the recession basket already +15.8% QTD vs SPX -1.2%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A downside Retail Sales print on Nov 17 that fuels the recession narrative.

tension_points.bull_case: Equity showed resilience last week to higher yields and bond vol. JPM thinks a 50bp December hike is highly unlikely and sees inflation as more of an early 2027 problem.
tension_points.bear_case: Hot Retail Sales plus hawkish Fedspeak (17 speakers) pushes talk of a 50bp hike, making the 4-hike pricing look too shallow and turning tightening risk into liquidity risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The market coming to believe a 50bp move is necessary.
